issues.title: Endermen teleports only when angry
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Passive Endermen

Minecraft version: 26.1.2 / 26.3
Modloader: Fabric

## **Feature description**
In my opinion, endermen should be able to teleport, but in some cases like enderman farms they tend to teleport out of the farm which lead me to using this mod. However, I think endermen should still have the ability to teleport, sinec that is basically what they're known for, so my suggestion is to add a config that lets endermen _only_ teleport if they are aggroed onto the player, so they won't teleport when they are angry towards an endermite. Oh and probably add more conditions like teleport when in water since your mod would disable their teleporting entirely, i just want my enderman farm to work whilst keeping their teleporting aspect :D

issues.title: All mods that haven't been updated since the config overhaul slow down title screen rendering
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Collective
Mod version: 8.57

Minecraft version: 26.3
Modloader: Fabric
Modloader version: 0.20.0
Environment: Both

## **Crash Report / Latest Log**
The latest.log file doesn't contain any relevant information at all, and the game doesn't crash.

## **Description**
Just as the title says, enabling/installing any mod that has not yet been updated since the most recent update to the Collective shared library causes the title screen to render very slowly. This issue is only worsened with each additional mod enabled, and can eventually lead to less than 5 FPS on the title screen with 10+ of your dependent mods enabled. All of your mods that have received updates as of today are unaffected; this issue is only affecting those of your mods which have not yet received updates since the release of Collective 8.57. Versions 8.56 and older of Collective did NOT exhibit this problem in any way, shape, or form. This issue ONLY appears on the main title screen, with the Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Options, and such buttons visible; going into ANY submenu (singleplayer world selection, options menu, multiplayer server selection, etc) immediately speed back up to a reasonable frame rate and do not show any symptoms. This issue doesn't show itself in server contexts either, no matter how many old mods are installed with the most recent version of Collective; it ONLY appears during the *MAIN* title screen in the client and NOWHERE ELSE.

In my small SMP server, I've noticed that giants that spawn naturally despawn rather fast, often under 10 seconds, before any player can properly approach them and initiate a chase or a battle.

issues.title: Allow dimension based multipliers for Altered Damage
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Altered Damage

Modloader: Fabric

## **Feature description**
A dimension based multiplier (including modded ones) would give modpack developers a lot more freedom.
A lot of dimension mods have hardcoded damage values and this mod would be perfect to deal with them.

For example in the Twilight Forest many projectiles damages are hardcoded so if a modpack gives stronger armor / buffs from other sources then the whole dimension is doing no damage to the player. This change would let modpacks better handle difficulty scaling. In these cases with a high global multiplier the endgame would still be challenging but the early game would become impossible.

The "dimension" based multiplier is a middle ground between Global and per-Entity multipliers which seemed easier to implement

issues.title: Natural World Generation for Custom Schematics
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.21.1+
Modloader: Other / All

## **Feature description**
Hi Serilum,  
I really like how easy Starter Structure makes it to use custom schematics,
and I was wondering if you would consider something similar for structures that generate naturally in the world,
either as a new feature or a separate mod.

The idea would be to simply drop an .nbt or .schem file into a folder.
The mod would detect it and automatically create the necessary configuration to make it a worldgen structure.

There could also be a default template config where you set things like rarity/spacing, biome tags, dimension, placement, rotation, etc.
New structures would use those settings when their individual configs are first generated,
and you could then adjust each structure separately if needed.

I thought the worldgen and structure configuration could perhaps be managed by Cristel Lib.
Since Starter Structure already has the functionality to import and read .nbt and .schem files,
I was thinking that part of the existing implementation could potentially be repurposed for importing the structures,
while Cristel Lib handles their natural world generation.

I think this could be really useful for modpack creators who want to quickly add their own structures without having to manually create all the corresponding datapack files.

Thanks for considering the idea ^^

issues.title: Tree Harvester Crashing MP Server
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Tree Harvester
Mod version: treeharvester-1.21.1-9.1

Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: NeoForge
Environment: Multiplayer

## **Crash Report / Latest Log**
https://gist.github.com/AliahMC/3adbac334504b2c4825b36d7330bca22

## **Description**
As an admin of the server, I was using Tree Harvester to take down some trees in a swamp with connecting leaves. If too many of the trees were too close together, then the log would not chop down and there were seconds before the server crashed. This happened a few times before we figured it out. We thought if we just didn't chop larger connected trees, we'd avoid problems. However, this problem shows up in another way, too.

The configs on the server are set to prevent Tree Harvester from breaking player-placed logs. One of our players made a log wall and then grew some additional trees on top. As the player's area grows and the wall is moved, the player is occasionally crouches to chop a part of the wall built in order to avoid falling off of the wall. The server immediately hangs and crashes, and will then go through a series of crashes every time that player comes online. The crash series is at least four iterations before we can stay online, again.

I have seen some folks requesting a feature that limits the number of logs that can be chopped, but that's a proposed solution to what is actually a bug. The mod should be property detecting one tree and should not be improperly chopping down player-placed logs. I don't know how the mod detects what is and is not a tree, but I'm happy to join in any conversation that discusses what this would look like and even test potential updates and fixes.

issues.title: Mod disables knockback from thrown projectiles (snowballs/eggs) on nearby entities, even without any teleport occurring
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: followersteleporttoo
Mod version: 26.1.2-2.8

Minecraft version: 26.1.2
Modloader: NeoForge
Modloader version: 26.1.2.109
Environment: Singleplayer

## **Description**
With Followers Teleport Too installed, thrown projectiles (snowballs and eggs) stop applying knockback to any entity they hit — including mobs that have never been teleported and even in freshly created worlds with no prior teleport commands used at all. Snow Golems throwing snowballs at Creepers produce zero knockback, and manually thrown snowballs/eggs by the player also produce zero knockback against any mob.

Steps to Reproduce
Set up a clean NeoForge 26.1.2 instance with only NeoForge + Followers Teleport Too + its required dependency (Collective) installed.

Create a new world.

Place a Snow Golem near a Creeper (or any hostile mob) and let it throw snowballs at it, OR manually throw a snowball/egg at any mob.

Observe that the mob receives no knockback whatsoever from the impact, despite vanilla behavior stating snowballs/eggs should still apply knockback even without dealing damage.

Expected Behavior
Per vanilla mechanics, snowballs and eggs should knock back mobs on impact (they just don't damage them, except Blazes). This should hold true regardless of whether any teleport command has ever been executed in the session.

Actual Behavior
No knockback is applied to any mob hit by a snowball or egg, even in scenarios with zero teleports performed. This suggests the mod's damage/knockback suppression logic (likely related to the disableFollowerDamageAfterTeleport config option, default true) is being applied too broadly — possibly to all nearby living entities rather than being scoped strictly to the player's own followers that were actually just teleported.

issues.title: Village Spawn Point Lag
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Village Spawn Point
Mod version: Version 4.6

Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: NeoForge
Modloader version: 21.1.250
Environment: Both

## **Question**
Hi, Serilum! I love your mod, Village Spawn Point, it feels like spawning right at home in RPG modpacks, so I always like to include it.

I have a question that I didn't see anyone talk about; It's about performance on spawn. But, before, here are a few affirmatives to understand the context:

- When spawning in a village, it's usually very laggy, especially on more modest computers.

- Villagers are well-known to be the most lag-inducing mobs.

- The most consuming tasks for villagers are POI and pathfinding.

- I know that it's not Village Spawn Point's fault.

- Some mods, like Liberty Villagers, allow you to reduce villagers' POI range, AI, etc., which allows for a smoother gameplay in villages.

- However, when spawning in the world, all villagers that spawn around the player perform their POI and other tasks simultaneously.

To deal with this issue, I see currently only two possible paths:

1. Keeping things as they are and accepting the significant lag when spawning.

2. Reducing a lot the POI/AI on Liberty Villagers' config so it lags less on startup at the cost of making villagers dumber/less exciting to interact with in the long run (after the startup).

So, I have this question: Would it be possible to add a config in the mod to make villagers' POI tasks start in groups instead of all at once, so the load spreads out on startup even if it takes a bit longer for villagers to get their professions? If that's not possible, how could we possibly mitigate this problem? Do you have any suggestions or ideas?

Thank you for your time and consideration.

issues.body: ## **Information** Mod name: Daily Quests Mod version: 26.3 Minecraft version: 26.3 Modloader: Fabric Modloader version: 26.3 Environment: Singleplayer ## **Crash Report / Latest Log** I tried to fix this on my own using Claude AI assistance. I copied the entire conversation of my problem with this Mod. Please read through and hopefully is helpful and can be fixed for future players like me. Screen shots were taken in this conversation but cannot be in this explanation, so understand that please while reading through this AI conversation. Thank you for your attention to this matter! Conversation with Claude AI starts Now: I am currently playing my Modded Minecraft, and I added Daily quests Mod and It doesn't seem to be working correctly. It says to hit the key button "." to close the intro. The key is not working. what should I do? 1790108676339_image.png that clearly did not work Searched the web I think we've hit the edge of what config settings alone can fix — this really does look like a bug in this particular version, since you've correctly changed both settings and it's still showing. That's not your fault or a mistake in what you did. A few honest options from here: Option 1 — Wait one in-game morning first. The mod's intro is designed to only show until the game reaches its first in-game morning, after which it's supposed to switch over to your actual 3 quests. If you haven't hit an in-game morning since installing this mod, it's technically possible the "stuck" intro is actually just... waiting for that to happen, and once it does, it may resolve itself regardless of the settings. An in-game day is about 20 real-world minutes — worth just playing normally for a bit to see if it clears once morning hits. Option 2 — Report it as a bug. Given you correctly changed both settings and neither worked, this looks like a genuine bug in version 2.9 of the mod. The mod's creator (Serilum) has a Discord and a CurseForge/Modrinth page with comments — reporting it there is the "real" fix path, since something's clearly not reading the config the way it should for your situation. Option 3 — Remove the mod. Since this is purely decorative and not blocking your gameplay, if it's more hassle than it's worth, you can disable or delete the mod from your mods list in Modrinth App. Just know that if you've already been given real daily quests before, removing the mod may lose that quest progress — but since you're stuck on the intro screen, that's likely not a concern for you. Given how much you've already tried, I'd lean toward trying Option 1 first since it costs you nothing — just keep playing for a bit and see if morning fixes it. Want to try that, or would you rather just remove the mod? maybe the mod itself it just totaly broken Addressing frustration with a simple next step. Addressing frustration with a simple next step. That's a completely reasonable conclusion at this point. You did everything right — checked the setting two different ways, confirmed the file saved, confirmed clean restarts — and it still didn't respond the way it should have. That's on the mod, not on you. Given that, I'd say don't sink more time into it. The simplest path: remove Daily Quests from your mods list in Modrinth App (the trash can icon next to it, or toggle it off), fully close and relaunch, and move on with your world. It's a nice-to-have feature, not something your world depends on, so losing it costs you nothing. If you want the annoyance gone permanently without pulling other mods along with it, removing just this one mod is safe — it won't affect Cuttable Wood, Cycle Paintings, or anything else in your list. can you do research if I am the only person to deal with this for this mod please? Searched the web Found the mod author's actual issue tracker — let me check it directly for similar reports. Searched the web, read a page I dug into this a bit more — the mod's creator (Serilum) actually keeps a centralized bug tracker on GitHub for all their mods, which is the "real" place people report issues like this. I searched through it but couldn't find an existing report that matches your exact situation (intro screen stuck on-screen even after disabling both the intro and the whole GUI via config). That doesn't necessarily mean you're the only one — it's possible other players just haven't reported it, gave up and uninstalled without saying anything, or it's specific to some interaction with another mod in your particular modpack (you've got a lot of mods installed, and mod conflicts causing weird GUI behavior like this aren't uncommon). But I can't point you to a confirmed matching bug report from someone else. Given that, if you want a "real" resolution rather than working around it, reporting it yourself on that GitHub tracker (linked from the mod's CurseForge/Modrinth page) would actually be useful — you have a clean, well-documented case (exact steps, screenshots, confirmed config values) that the developer could act on. But that's optional; removing the mod is a completely reasonable path if you'd rather just move on and keep playing. ## **Description**

## **Information**
Mod name: Starter Structure
Mod version: 4.2

Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Forge
Modloader version: 47.4.10
Environment: Both

## **Description**
Using a datapack to make respawn anchors work in the overworld and be the only method to respawn.
Having forceExactSpawn be enabled, makes the respawn anchor use up two charges when respawning.
Should the anchor be at one charge, the player will briefly appear at it before teleporting to world spawn, suggesting the respawn logic is being run twice.

In StructureSpawnPointEvents there is a call to Player.findRespawnPositionAndUseSpawnBlock
This is not intended to just find the player's respawn position as it actually drains a charge from the anchor.

While not tested, Set World Spawn Point uses the same logic, so i would assume it can cause the same issues.

Broken tools are not replaced from the inventory. Breaking a wooden shovel while holding an identical wooden shovel in the inventory does nothing, no replacement and no error in the log. Collective 8.39 is installed, so the dependency requirement is met.

issues.title: [Mineral Chance] Configurable Drop Weights for Individual Minerals
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Mineral Chance

Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: Fabric

## **Feature description**
First off - Love this mod a lot! It definitely makes mining through boring blocks much more interesting.

My biggest concern about this mod is that it can make some ores far too easy to acquire. Diamonds, Emeralds, Netherite Scrap, having them drop in the same frequency as gold and iron nuggets just doesn't seem right.

I was trying to think if there is any simple way to add a configurable chance to each potential mineral. Currently the configuration allows to customize the chance to getRandomOverworldMineral and the nether equivalent, so I went looking through the UTIL section and found where the random mineral chance is being generated from on the lines:
public class Util {
	private static final List<Item> overworldminerals = new ArrayList<Item>(Arrays.asList(Items.DIAMOND, Items.GOLD_NUGGET, Items.IRON_NUGGET, Items.LAPIS_LAZULI, Items.REDSTONE, Items.EMERALD));
	private static final List<Item> netherminerals = new ArrayList<Item>(Arrays.asList(Items.QUARTZ, Items.GOLD_NUGGET, Items.NETHERITE_SCRAP));

Just in looking at this, I can tell a feature like this would turn something that is designed to be a simple static list into a much more complicated process.

But I thought I would suggest it anyway. 

What do you think, is there a simple way to change this array to give weights to the random chance of each individual type of mineral that could be customized in the config? Honestly it would also be nice to have a way to add and remove minerals from this array through the config so that modded minerals could also be added to the drop chance for this mod. But I think the best next step for this mod would be a custom drop weight to keep rarer minerals rare.

Thank for everything you do!

issues.title: healingcampfire and nohostilesaroundcampfire server crash
issues.body:
> **[Updated root cause — 2026-08-01]** _(Earlier mentions of Lithium/ServerCore were a red herring; disregard.)_

**TL;DR — packaging lag.** The campfire mods were already fixed on 2026-06-29 (Healing Campfire **6.3**, No Hostiles Around Campfire **7.4**), but the latest **Serilum's RPG Bundle 2.9 (2026-06-21)** still embeds the pre-fix **6.2 / 7.2**. Any pack on Collective ≥8.38 + the current bundle hits this crash. **Ask: republish the RPG bundle (e.g. 2.10) embedding HC 6.3 / NHaC 7.4.**

**Mechanism** — the `WeakReference`s come from **Collective itself**, not optimization mods:
- **Collective 8.38 (2026-06-29)** changed `BlockEntityData.cachedBlockEntities` from `CopyOnWriteArrayList<BlockEntity>` → `CopyOnWriteArrayList<WeakReference<BlockEntity>>` (a memory-leak fix) and added a new `getCachedBlockEntities()` API that dereferences.
- Java **generic type erasure** hides the change at link/load time, so old 6.2/7.2 still load — but throw `ClassCastException: WeakReference cannot be cast to BlockEntity` when the for-each loop casts each entry. That is the crash at `CampfireEvent.playerTickEvent(:37)` and `onEntityCheckSpawn(:89)`.
- The same-day **6.3 / 7.4** updates simply switch to calling the new dereferencing API.

**Workarounds until the bundle is republished:**
1. Disable `enableHealingCampfire` / `enableNoHostilesAroundCampfire` in the bundle config, or
2. Downgrade **Collective to 8.32** (last build before the `WeakReference` change) — bundle 6.2/7.2 then work as designed.

---

Before disabling both mods:

More telling server log:

## **Description**
NeoForge-1.21.1-233
serilumsrpgbundle-1.21.1-2.9.jar
healingcampfire and nohostilesaroundcampfire server crash
disabling both mods resolved the crashing

Full mod list:

[OurGame-1.21.1_v2_mods_server.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29511390/OurGame-1.21.1_v2_mods_server.txt)

Gemini suggested the following being the problem (based on the 'More telling server logs'):

```
Error Breakdown

The server crash is caused by a ClassCastException originating from the Healing Campfire mod (version 6.2) running on NeoForge for Minecraft 1.21.1.

    The Technical Issue: The mod's code attempts to cast a Java WeakReference object directly into a Minecraft BlockEntity object during the playerTickEvent routine. This is an invalid Java operation; the code must dereference the WeakReference first to access the underlying entity.

    Point of Failure: The stack trace explicitly identifies the broken code at com.natamus.healingcampfire_common_neoforge.events.CampfireEvent.playerTickEvent(CampfireEvent.java:37).

```

And second crash (before removing no hostiles around campfire)

```
Error Breakdown

The server experienced an identical ClassCastException to your previous crash. However, the point of failure has shifted to a different mod: No Hostiles Around Campfire (version 7.2).

The stack trace points to com.natamus.nohostilesaroundcampfire_common_neoforge.events.CampfireEvent.onEntityCheckSpawn(CampfireEvent.java:89). Both this mod and the previous "Healing Campfire" mod are created by the same developer (Serilum / com.natamus). They share the same flawed logic for casting WeakReference objects directly to BlockEntity within NeoForge 1.21.1 campfire events.
```

issues.title: Suggestion -- This or That
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Configurable Extra Mob Drops

Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: Forge

## **Feature description**
To start, mod works wonderfully, and I can't find anything as good on CF for Forge 1.21.1, and my friends are using it on a project we're doing and love it. (:

But I was curious if it would be possible to implement a feature for determining the drop rate of specific item(s) over another from mobs (vanilla or modded) when adjusting the loot-table. 

When playing with mods that drop lots of options or two very similar items from a mob, having even both items with .01 still has several instances of them both dropping--and while that can be nice, sometimes we just want it to drop one or the other.

We want to have lots of replay-ability, but when both are a guarantee or have similar drop chances that trigger simultaneously (not to say it isn't funny or nice to have both in one fell swoop)--It could be helpful to have it pick between options. So, either the mob upon death drops ABC or XYZ, but not both ABC and XYZ. The chance of either is still the same (or to whatever a person's set them to), just you don't get both...?

A terrible example but:
ABC is a .1% chance, and XYZ is a .5% chance -- when the mob is killed it picks between the two items (ABC or XYZ) and then drops that one. 
Like the vanilla goat horn has 8 options (4 normal/4 yelling), you can only get up to 2 in an adult, but they'll be the same type (two sing, two call, etc.).--It picks the type and you can get lucky and get more of that type (the mod already has implementation for the amount a drop can be based on how many was in your hand when the command was set, so that doesn't need any change.), but you're not getting the other 3 possible horns from that goat you'd have to find another--adding that replay-ability we're after.
That feature from the goats just as a more widespread feature...

issues.title: [1.16.5 Fabric 3.3] Dispenser bonemeal still uses vanilla biome flower noise
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Random Bone Meal Flowers
Mod version: 3.3

Minecraft version: 1.16.5
Modloader: Fabric
Modloader version: 0.16.14
Environment: - Minecraft Version: 1.16.5
- Mod Version: Random Bone Meal Flowers 1.16.5-3.3-fabric
- Mod Loader: Fabric
- Dependencies: Latest Fabric API + Collective

## **Description**
This mod successfully randomizes flowers when players use bone meal manually.
However, bone meal fired from a **dispenser** still follows the vanilla coordinate-based noise function in Flower Forest biomes. The flowers spawned are fixed per position, which does not get randomized.

I noticed the changelog states "Fixed dispensers not randomizing flower spawns", but this fix is incomplete for the 1.16.5 Fabric build.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install Fabric loader, Fabric API, Collective and this mod.
2. Locate a Flower Forest biome.
3. Use bone meal by hand on grass blocks → flowers spawn randomly (works correctly).
4. Place a dispenser filled with bone meal and activate it → flowers spawn based on vanilla coordinate rules (bug occurs).

## Expected Behavior
Flowers generated by dispenser bone meal should also be fully random, just like player-used bone meal, and ignore the original position-based generation logic.

issues.title: Have a single, particular, block that still blocks the beam
issues.body:
## **Information**
Mod name: Underground Beacons

Minecraft version: 26.1.2
Modloader: Fabric

## **Feature description**
Right now no block can stop the beacon from activating. This is very useful in cases where we are mining underground and want to very quickly set up the beacon or when we have a beacon in a certain specific position and we decide to build above it while still having the beacons effects. I would argue, however, that having a single, very particular, block that still stops the beacon is useful in some situations. In my particular case I cannot move the beacon, I have a build above it so this mod allows me to have the effects always active, but I want to control (activate/deactivate) them with redstone and in no way I can stop them with the current implementation. An idea for a block to do so could be the tinted glass block.

## **Description**
Welcome to All The ~~Mods~~ Issues!
**Does "All the Issues" really contain ALL THE ISSUES? I don't know, maybe?**

Today I tried to cycle a painting, but I noticed an extra painting was dropping out of the wall every time I cycled. Also, cycling a 4-block tall painting would cause it to move a block upwards. After some testing, I found out none of these issues triggered when the painting overlapped with another block (chests, flower pots, etc), however an overlapped painting that's 4 blocks tall and 3 blocks wide won't cycle at all (despite having more than one variant available). 

I found this issue while playing in a multiplayer server, so I loaded a singleplayer world in order to submit a more detailed report. issues.title: Entity dies if it fails to transform
issues.body:
Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: Fabric
Mod name: Overworld Piglins

If the weakness effect expires before the piglin/hoglin transforms, it gradually takes damage and dies. Kinda makes sense for the Overworld, but occurs in the Nether as well, since they don't zombify there.

issues.title: Dimmensional Passive Enderman
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.19.2
Modloader: Forge (43.5.0)

Mod name: Passive Endermen


## **Feature description**
I've had this amazing idea!
What if we could configure Endemen behavior per biome/dimension. I originally thought of this as just restricting it to dimensions, but I can see someone asking for dimension-filtering capabilities.
Here's my original thought: I want to disable grieving and aggro on the overworld and aggro on the nether. The mod already deactivates griving and aggro plus teleportation. So the idea would be to be able to configure behavior based on the dimension the enderman is located. I hope this doesn't break out of the scope of the mod.

Thanks for reading!

issues.body:
## **Information**

Modloader: Fabric

Environment: Multiplayer

Mod name: Random Bone Meal Flowers
Mod version: 1.21.11-4.7


## **Description**
Hello, my friend and I are playing on a server I am hosting using the Fabric loader. We both launch our clients through curseforge. I've tried installing the mod on only the server, no change in flower generation. I've tried loading into singleplayer, no change. We've tried both downloading it on the clients, and launching with it installed on the server. No luck!

We also have Terralith on our world. We have quite a few other mods, about 50, but most of them are very light- not huge additions to the game. Could Terralith be the reason the flowers aren't changing? We have both collective and infinite trading installed (Serilum mods) which work perfectly.

issues.title: Non-Critical Bug in Ore Harvester
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.21.10
Modloader: Neoforge
NeoForge version: 21.10.64
Environment: Both

Mod name: Ore Harvester
Mod version: 1.5


## **Description**
A logic flaw in the **Ore Harvester** mod allows players to bypass the intended mining speed penalty (which should scale based on vein size) when vein-mining. 

Currently, the mod calculates the increased mining time based on whether the player is crouching. However, the check for the "vein-mine" trigger occurs at the moment of the block break, while the "mining speed" penalty is only applied if the player is crouching *during* the mining process. This allows a player to mine at normal speed and "tap" crouch at the last second to trigger the harvest.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Locate a large ore vein.
2. Begin mining a single block **without** crouching (maintaining the tool's default mining speed).
3. Just before the block break animation completes (at the "last moment"), press and hold the **Crouch/Shift** key.
4. The block finishes breaking while the player is crouching.

### Observed Result
The entire vein is harvested instantly (or at the speed of a single block), completely ignoring the "increased time to mine" penalty described in the mod’s documentation. The player receives the benefits of the vein-mine without the "mega-slow" trade-off.

### Expected Result
The mining speed should be calculated based on the intent to vein-mine. If a player triggers a vein-mine, the time taken should reflect the total number of blocks in that vein, regardless of when the crouch key was pressed during the break animation.

---

### Reference Documentation
> "Ore Harvester allows players to mine entire ore veins instantly, by breaking one of the blocks in it while crouching. **The time it takes to mine is increased by the amount of ore that's in the vein.**"

### User Conversation Summary
* **BaoBuns:** "if you don't shift on the block you breaking till you're about to break it you can vein mine it without the speed penalty"
* **Kree Zill:** "so you're saying just beat on the block normally and then at last moment before it would harvest, hold shift and wala the hole things mines without the mega-slow..."
* **BaoBuns:** "bingo you got it"


## **Crash report**
There is no crashing.

issues.title: Infinite trading: setting `maxUses` to INT_MAX can be dangerous for integer overflow.
issues.body:
Recently I installed Infinite Trading mod and unstalled this mod after some trading in my Single Player world, that means I played MC without this mod.
Then interesting thing happened after several days in game: prices grow up to 64 emeralds, however sometimes it fall back to 1.

There are similar problems in the issue tracker and of course they have been solved years ago, the solution is simply set `demand` to 0 so price will never blow up. So I look into the code...

Anyway, if I continue playing with this mod uninstalled, bad thing around `maxUses = INT_MAX` happened, this makes `demand` grow up gradually. In vanilla MC, `demand` changes when villagers restock, as pseudo-code below:

```java
demand = demand + uses - (maxUses - uses)
```

Villagers restocks everyday, including days that player doesn't trade, so `uses`  is 0 in code above, that is: `demand -= maxUses`

Infinite Trading rewrites villagers' NBT, making `maxUses` up to INT_MAX, let's say `demand` is 0 at the beginning, after somd restocks:

1. demand = -INT_MAX
2. demand = 2
3. demand = -INT_MAX + 2
4. demand = 4
...

It's clear that demand is increasing even the player does nothing, thanks to the integer overflow caused by INT_MAX.

I encountered this problem when playing game without this mod, so I don't think this is a bug of mod itself, but is something need to talk about? My suggestion is change `maxUses` from INT_MAX to some number that is large enough for "infinite trading" feel, while is safe enough to avoid integer overflow bugs, e.g. `100,000`.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Option to disable Welcome Message for first-time players
issues.body:
## Description
I'm using both **First Join Message** and **Welcome Message** mods together. 

Currently, when a new player joins the server for the first time, they see BOTH messages:
1. First Join Message: "Welcome for the first time..."
2. Welcome Message: "Welcome back..."

This creates a confusing situation where new players see "Welcome back" on their first visit.

## Suggested Solution
Could you add a config option in Welcome Message to:
- Disable the message for players on their first join
- Or add a condition check to skip if it's the player's first time

Example config:
```json5
"skipFirstTimeJoins": true  // Don't show welcome message if it's player's first join
```

## Alternative Solution
Or add a placeholder/variable support like:
```json5
"messageOneText": "{first_join ? 'Welcome!' : 'Welcome back!'}"
```

## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Fabric

Mod name: First Join Message
                   Welcome Message


## **Feature description**
I've had this amazing idea!

## Additional Context
Both mods work great individually! Just looking for better integration when used together.

Thank you for your amazing mods! 🙏

Minecraft version: 1.21.11

## **Description**
I just updated my game & all my mods from 1.21.8 to 1.21.11. As I always do when updating, before loading my long-term world save I loaded a test-world to make sure that mods were still working in the updated version. The world loaded fine, and other mods were working. But when I tried using bonemeal on the ground, the only flowers produced were Dandelion, Poppy, Oxeye Daisy, Cornflower, Azure Bluet, & maybe some Tulips. This was in a plains biome, and those are all the flowers that are produced by bonemealing the ground in plains biomes in Vanilla minecraft. It was as if this mod wasn't installed at all. 
I'd been using this mod for my main save in 1.21.8 and it worked perfectly then. I'd even used it when I made this same test-world when I first updated to 1.21.8 and it worked there too; I remember because the flowers produced from testing it were still left where they'd been grown in a cluster, including some Alliums & Eyeblossoms.
I checked the blacklist config file for this world and nothing had a "!" in front of it other than Wither Rose (which I assume was by default since those never got produced in my main world even though I wanted them), so the blacklist is not the problem.

There was no crash or error message.

issues.title: Naturally spawning Silverfish
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.16.5
Modloader: Forge

This mod would introduce naturally spawning blocks that are already infested with silverfish throughout the world. The goal is to bring more attention to an often overlooked game mechanic while adding an extra layer of challenge and unpredictability to exploration. Encountering infested blocks unexpectedly would make mining and dungeon exploration more engaging and slightly more dangerous, enhancing overall gameplay without drastically changing the vanilla experience. 

The mod should include a configurable value that allows server owners and players to adjust the spawn chance of infested block veins / single infected blocks, making it easy to balance difficulty to their preference.

While I personally play on version 1.16.5, I believe this mod would also be well received if it were available for other Minecraft versions as well, allowing a wider range of players to enjoy the feature.

issues.title: Tree Harvester - Proposal to Change Tree Harvest Speed Equation
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Forge / Fabric

Mod name: Tree Harvester


## **Feature description**
Hi there and Happy New Year, 

Would you be interested in updating the mod to change the equation for increasing harvest time per log: 

I would like for big trees to take significantly longer to cut than the small trees, but can only get fast logging times with the current equation 

the current equation is: 
   newSpeed = originalSpeed / (1 + (logCount * increasedHarvestingTimePerLogModifier)).

the equation I'd like to propose is: 
   newSpeed = originalSpeed * logCount * increasedHarvestingTimePerLogModifier 

I had a sad moment where I was building a multi-tree tree house, and when I went to strip some bark off the log, I shift right clicked by mistake... 
in like half a second, I ended up cutting down the massive tree :(
Devastating

Having the cutting speed directly proportional to the modifier would let me set the speed to be much longer for big trees, and hopefully avoid this 
It should still be possible to have fast logging times too, for those who prefer that 

e.g. 
want low logging time, use low modifier (0.02)

= original speed * logcount * 0.02

want longer cutting time, use higher modifier (10) 

= original speed * logcount * 10

If see any issues with this equation just let me know 

Other than this, the mod has been a great addition to my gameplay, so thank you for making and sharing! 

Thanks!

issues.title: [Fabric 1.21.1] Repeated elytra damage sound during flight & firework takeoff not working underwater (with Accessories ecosystem)
issues.body:
Environment

Minecraft: 1.21.1

Loader: Fabric

Mod: Easy Elytra Takeoff

Collective: installed (latest)

Related mods in use:

Accessories (Fabric)

Accessories Compat Layer

Accessorify
(All versions are for 1.21.1)

Issue 1: Repeated elytra damage sound during normal flight

Description
When using Easy Elytra Takeoff on Fabric 1.21.1, the elytra plays a breaking/durability damage sound repeatedly at about 1-second intervals while flying, even when simply gliding normally.

Expected behavior

Elytra durability should decrease normally

Damage sound should only play when appropriate (not repeatedly during flight)

Actual behavior

While flying with elytra, the damage sound keeps playing repeatedly

This happens continuously during flight

It feels like the elytra flight start logic is being triggered repeatedly

Notes

No crash or error in logs

The mod itself loads correctly

The issue persists even when Accessorify is not actively used in gameplay

This behavior does not occur in 1.21.8, only in 1.21.1

Issue 2: Firework takeoff does not work underwater (1.21.1)

Description
One of the core features of Easy Elytra Takeoff is that using a firework should immediately force elytra flight regardless of player state (including underwater).
This behavior is shown in videos and worked correctly in previous versions.

However, in 1.21.1, using a firework while underwater does not trigger elytra takeoff.

Expected behavior

Using a firework while wearing an elytra should force elytra flight

This should work even underwater

Actual behavior

Firework is consumed

Player does not enter elytra flight when underwater

Additional context

These issues appear only on Fabric 1.21.1

They do not happen on 1.21.8 with the same mod setup

The repeated damage sound suggests startFallFlying() or equivalent logic may be triggered multiple times during flight

The underwater firework issue may be related to changed elytra state checks in 1.21.1

Request

Could you please:

Check for repeated elytra flight start logic during active flight in Fabric 1.21.1

Restore or fix underwater firework-triggered elytra takeoff behavior for 1.21.1

If possible, confirm whether this is a known Fabric 1.21.1 behavioral change

## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Fabric
Fabric loader version: 0.17.2
Environment: Multiplayer
Mod name: Realistic Bees

## **Description**
Server crashed with a NullPointerException when a player broke a beehive block. The crash occurs in the `BeeNestDestroyedCriterion$Conditions.handler$gkd000$realisticbees$matches` method at line 520. 

The error indicates that `NumberRange$IntRange.getMin()` is returning null, and the code is attempting to call `.intValue()` on this null value without checking for null first. This causes the advancement criterion check to fail and crash the server.

The crash is 100% reproducible when breaking beehives/bee nests.

issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.21.10
Modloader: Fabric

Environment: Multiplayer

Mod names: Ore Harvester and Tree Harvester
Mod version: 1.5 and 9.3


## **Problem/Question**
I've set up my own Linux Minecraft server and since then the aforementioned two mods no longer work as expected. When we (the people I play with) cut down trees or mine ore there's some weird behaviour:
We hit the blocks with a tool until it is considered destroyed. Then the block disappears for a fraction of a second, reappears just as if the server said "nope, not going to happen", and then roughly a second later the tree/vein disappears and all drops spawn.
If we instead just break the blocks individually everything is working as expected.

This delay didn't happen on the Aternos server we played on previously - to be fair, I also used a (slightly) different mod setup on there. I tried the mods in single player with the exact same (current) mod setup in place. In SP there's no delay. Then I tried disabling various mods that sounded like they might have an influence on the Harvester mods. No success so far. I tried a different tree cutting mod and that one was working as expected, no delay, everything happened immediately and felt snappy. I also checked the server log for hints at what is going on, but no indicator in there either. And the world runs very smooth otherwise so it can't be the server being overloaded.

issues.title: Beautified Chat [Client] does not handle server messages on 1.21.x (and likely also 1.20.x)
issues.body:
Heya! I'm working on a mod that bridges chat messages with Zulip (a selfhostable discord-like chat platform), and noticed that while on older versions (e.g. 1.18.2), the mods work perfectly together - on newer versions (that use the chat report / verified profile system) the messages no longer get parsed by BC[C].

I had a peek in Collective and saw that `CollectiveChatEvents.CLIENT_CHAT_RECEIVED` hooks `showMessageToPlayer`, which is fired for `handlePlayerChatMessage`, but not for `handleDisguisedChatMessage`.

I did not find a way to construct a message on the server side that causes the client to invoke `showMessageToPlayer`, as all messages of unknown players get discarded / fail verification, even with chat reports disabled.

Any input would be appreciated.

issues.title: Force Exact Spawn Set To Corner Of Block, Not Its Center
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: NeoForge
NeForge version: 21.1.216
Environment: Singleplayer

Mod name: Set World Spawn
Mod version: 3.5


## **Description**
When you spawn normally, you do so in the center of the block.  To be more precise, you do so at coordinates XX.5, YY.0, ZZ.5, which is to say that your X anx Z coordinates are not integer numbers, but floats with a decimal value of .5, which is why you appear in the center of the block, and not at some other point, as you can stand at any point on the block, and thus there are coordinate values for any location on a block.

When using the "Force Exact Spawn" rule of this mod, one would expect that they would be able to specify the exact block one would spawn on, which one can, but one would also expect to spawn in the middle of said chosen block, not barely standing on the very corner, where one might, for example, end up spawning inside of some other adjacent block.

The Solution:
There is no need to allow players to inter floating point numbers for X and Z coordinates, just simply convert said integer coordinates to floats and add "0.5" to them when using the "Force Exact Spawn" rule.


## **Crash report**
No Crashes, just incorrect behavior...

issues.title: Crouch-Toggle Instant Harvest Exploit
issues.body:
I am currently hosting a multiplayer server and there's a _major_ exploit that allows you to instantly harvest any tree of any size by simply toggling crouch while breaking the first log block of a given tree. Here's how it works:

- Find the base of the tree you want to cut down
- Hold crouch and hold left click to begin breaking the block like normal
- Interrupt the action by releasing crouch while still holding down left click

You'll break the block normally as you would through single-block harvesting based on what axe you're using, (without the additional time added by crouch-harvesting the full tree) but still cut down the entire tree as though you were crouching the whole time.

What's also strange is, this instant-cut state may be "**stored**" between trees. If you repeat this process: crouch, hold down left click on any tree, then stop both actions without breaking the block, walk to a completely separate tree, and cut one of its logs normally with left click, it will immediately harvest the entire tree as though you were crouching, thereby skipping all of the time that's normally supposed to be added depending upon how many logs a tree has.

This bug is easily replicated in every version I tested, though I am currently using 1.20.1.

**Edit**: Alternatively, if you activate "Tree Harvest Without Sneak" whereby all trees cut down normally will utilize the mod and logs cut from a crouching position will be cut normally, you simply have to apply this toggle in reverse and the exploit functions the same: begin cutting down a tree, then quickly switch to crouch to finish cutting and you negate **ALL** "Harvesting Time Per Log".

issues.title: New mod fixing randomness of world generation
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: all versions or atleast popular ones like 1.12.2, 1.16.5, 1.19.4, 1.20.1
Modloader: Forge and Fabric


## **Feature description**
My biggest problem with Minecraft is that there is no guarantee that you will find desired biome or structure after walking thousands of blocks due to RNG. Worlds feel monotonous and empty because of vast uninteresting territory between your base and unreasonably rare places.
I suggest you to make a new mod that adds limited world type where biomes and structures are not randomly generated but randomly placed in specific quantity across the map with configurable size. In small diverse worlds players will be more motivated to use maps, build roads and railways etc.
If this is too hard to implement then you can make different mod adding new command that runs invisible "locate" commands for all biomes and structures. If some coordinates are too far then mod says that current world is bad or what structures and biomes are too far. This is much easier to make but players will have to check multiple seeds.

issues.title: Thoughts about Licenses
issues.body:
**This message was refactored using ChatGPT and double-checked to ensure it accurately reflects my genuine opinion.
(English is still a work in progress for me, so I wanted to make my thoughts as clear as possible.)**

Hello,

I truly appreciate your work — it’s exceptionally well-coded and thoughtfully designed. However, I noticed that all your projects are currently licensed as Copyrighted content.

While it’s completely understandable to want to protect the results of your hard work (and as a fellow developer, I fully understand your point of view), I’d like to kindly suggest that you consider adopting an open-source license — perhaps something GPL3.0-like — at least for your Collective Library.

Here’s my perspective on this:

Allowing others to benefit from your work — even from a “small” part of it — can create a positive feedback loop, especially considering that Collective is such a large and impactful project.

When people are able to learn from or build upon your work, they often respond with genuine appreciation and support, which can also benefit you in return.

issues.title: Nether Portal Spread "Invasion"
issues.body:
Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Forge / Fabric

Mod name: Nether Portal Spread


I've had an idea that I'm sure has been suggested to you, but I still think it would be an awesome idea. The way the mod is now, there isn't really too much of a reason to stop the spread of the nether corruption. since it just changes blocks in a radius. If it's in your base that's understandable, but out in the world, there isn't really any problem if the configs aren't set to spread across the entire world. I have a few ideas to change that.

1) Mobs spawn in the radius of nether portal corruption. I don't just mean Zombified Piglins, but rather almost all mobs the nether contains are viable to spawn. Piglins could spawn in raiding parties, and remain unzombified as long as they stay within the portal corruption. Ghasts will sometimes spawn above if the area is big enough. the normal things you would expect if the nether was to invade the overworld.

2) Nether mobs will begin to build around the portal. They know that if the portal gets destroyed, the Piglins will zombify, and their invasion will be forced to end. I can see the invading Piglins building a stronghold around the portal given enough time, and building blaze spawners, along with their towers. Maybe they'll put empty chests down, as if preparing a place to stash their haul.

3) Portal spread will have tiers. All the things that I mentioned wouldn't happen right away. Mob spawning, and protection from zombification would happen when the portal reaches tier 2. Tier 3 is when the Piglins start building defenses The portal also becomes more ingrained, and leaves behind a portal essence which will restart the portal if the blocks remain. Tier 4 even more mobs, and the portal is almost at full strength, and is spreading further and more rapidly. Tier 5 is when the Portal is at full power, and is also at it's most difficult to contain. The spread has stopped (unless configs say otherwise), but the portal obsidian will reform if broken, destroy everything in the way of recreating the portal, dry up liquids in close proximity to it (placing water acts as if placing it in the nether), and is far more expensive to contain.

4) Portal tiers make it more expensive to contain the spread, with each tier requiring the materials from the previous tier, and requiring more the stronger the portal grows before you take action. Tier 1 can be contained with just 4 coal blocks. Tier 2 requires 4 iron blocks extra, Tier 3 requires an additional 2 gold blocks, Tier 4 requires 1 diamond block and 2 emerald blocks. Tier 5 is the toughest to contain, requiring a beacon. If you manage to contain the full strength portal, then you can finally close it. Leaving a stabilized level 5 portal would however provide benefits, with the nether mobs being pacified, and maybe even providing tribute?

I just think it would really help the feeling of the nether invading the world through the portals, and encourage preparation for opening a portal.

issues.title: Starter Structure: Config Option to Set the Structure's Generation Dimension
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Forge / Fabric

Mod name: Starter Structure


Hello!

I have a suggestion that I believe would be a good feature for custom modpack creation.

The Problem:
When creating a modpack that changes the player's initial spawn dimension (using mods like "Initial Dimension" or the feature within "Origins"), the starting structure still generates in the Overworld by default. This means that if a player is meant to spawn in a different dimension, the intended starting structure is not there with them.

My Suggestion:
I would like to suggest adding a configuration option that allows modpack creators to define which dimension the structure should generate in.

How It Could Work:
In the mod's config file, there could be a parameter to specify the dimension's ID. For example, instead of it being hardcoded to minecraft:overworld, a user could change it to another dimension's ID (e.g., ad_astra:mars).

Why This is a Great Feature ☝️🤓:
This would be an incredibly powerful tool for modpack creators for a few key reasons:

Thematic Starts: It enables truly immersive starting experiences. For example, a space-themed modpack could have the player start in a base on another planet (using a dimension from a mod like Ad Astra). 

Another use case is a modpack I'm making, where the player "dies" and must first escape a limbo/underworld dimension, where the starting structure would be located.

Where the structure is suposed to spawn:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7547deaa-f8bc-4f64-a3cb-e1ff7b6d32c5)

Where it actually spawns:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abdba0c3-7b84-4c83-b58e-07935a706e7c)


I don't have much experience with mod development, so I'm not sure how difficult this would be to implement, but I believe it would be a cool feature for modpack-making.

I translated the text from Portuguese to English with AI, I hope it is understandable lol.

issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1

First mod name: Tree Harvester 
First mod version: 1.20.1-9.1

Second mod version: flan-1.20.1-1.11.14


## **Description**

hello, i hope you're doing well !!

tldr of what flan does just in case: allows you to designate an area as 'yours', and there's various permissions you can toggle, one of which is the ability to break blocks. 

essentially, if there's a log block outside of the designated area that is connected to log block(s) inside the area, when that external log block is mined, the one(s) inside will also be destroyed, even if the person doing so doesn't have permission to break blocks within that designated area. 

this is an extremely niche issue, so i completely understand if asking for mod compatibility is unrealistic. i just figured it wouldn't hurt to ask, since both of the mods involved are very popular, and i'm probably not the only one who plays a modpack with both mods, so it might help others. 

in any case, thank you for reading this !! ~

issues.title: Hangs indefinitely if no village can be generated
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 21.1
Modloader: NeoForge
Forge version: 200
Environment: Singleplayer 

Mod name: Village Spawn point
Mod version: 1.21.1-4.6


## **Description**
I am working on a challenge mode for my modpack (which uses Village Spawn Point), in that challenge mode a noise generator is used to turn the entire world into a flat world and also remove all structures. When selecting that world type Village Spawn Point starts to search for a village but cannot find any as none are generated. Effectively world generation hangs indefinitely.

Two things should be changed:
- If the world does not generate village structures this mod should not search for any.
- If searching for a village takes longer than x seconds (configurable?) it should abort and use the usual spawn.

## **Crash report**
latest.log clearly shows that this mod is the issue, this is the last entry before world generation hangs up:
`[Server thread/INFO] [com.natamus.villagespawnpoint_common_neoforge.events.VillageSpawnEvent/]: [Village Spawn Point] Finding the nearest village. This might take a few seconds.`

Disabling the mod immediately fixes the issue.

issues.title: Enhancement: Assign gender-appropriate names to villagers
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Forge 

Mod name: Villager Names


## **Feature description**
I've had this amazing idea! I'm using the Human Era Villagers resource pack, which adds more human-like villagers and introduces gender distinctions, including female villagers. While using this alongside the Villager Names mod, I noticed that the names assigned to villagers don't reflect their gender—female villagers often receive traditionally male names and vice versa.
It would be a fantastic enhancement if Villager Names could detect or integrate with gendered villagers and assign names accordingly. This would greatly improve immersion and roleplay potential, especially for modpacks that emphasize realism or storytelling.

Possible Implementation Ideas:

- Add optional gender-based name lists (e.g., female_names.txt, male_names.txt) that users can customize.
- Detect gender tags from compatible mods or resource packs like Human Era Villagers and assign names from the appropriate list.
- Include a fallback or toggle for users who prefer gender-neutral naming.

Thanks for all your work on this mod—it’s a small detail, but it makes a big difference in the world-building experience!

issues.title: Request to fix MC-226687 (sea level assumed to be y=63)
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: NeoForge


## **Feature description**
https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC/issues/MC-226687

The sea level is assumed to be y=63 for various mechanics, including mob spawning. So if you raise the sea level to anything higher, nothing will spawn there; even modded creatures that use this code. Mods that allow for modifying spawns tend to be janky and overly methodical. Fish will unnaturally spawn in and out of existence. A mod like this, that addresses the core issue, would open the gateway to better ocean-themed modpacks.

This bug was fixed in 1.21.2 but most major content mods have no reason to port to this version.

I'm aware this is hardcoded into what I believe are base classes, and I understand you cannot modify those (and be on good terms with Forge), but are there other ways to address this?

I closed it bc I made my own

issues.title: Crash: ConcurrentModificationException when used with C2ME
issues.body:
## **Information**

Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: Fabric
Fabric loader version: 0.16.14
Environment: Singleplayer (Opened to LAN)

Mod name: Random Village Names
Mod version: 3.8

## **Description**

Hey! My game becomes very unstable and eventually crashes when using Random Village Names alongside the performance mod C2ME (Concurrent Chunk Management Engine).

The server thread log gets spammed with `ConcurrentModificationException` errors pointing to the `SetVillageSignEvent.onWorldTick` event in your mod. ## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1 - 1.21.5
Modloader: Fabric

Mod name: Grindstone Sharper Tools


## **Feature description**
So, first of all, I want to take this opportunity to thank you for creating these mods and in the way you do, you've been a huge inspiration and one of the reasons I got into modding in the first place.  
Now, a user of my own mod "_More Grindstone Variants_" came to me asking for compatibility with "_Grindstone Sharper Tools_". (pnk2u/More-Grindstone-Variants#7)  
I assumed correctly that the issue they can't use the mod's newly added _Sharpening_ functionality with my _Grindstone Variants_ is that _Grindstone Sharper Tools_ checks for the Block (``block.equals(Blocks.GRINDSTONE)``) instead of checking for the Block class (``block instanceof GrindstoneBlock``) which I tend to favor and would prevent the incompatibility.
Do you think this would be possible to change on your end and release an update or is there some issue with that I'm missing? Otherwise I'd have to Mixin into your GrindEvent class which is possible but I'd really like to not have to do that. :D

issues.body:
## **Information**

Modloader: Fabric
Fabric loader version: 0.16.14
Environment: Singleplayer

Mod name: Configurable Extra Mob Drops
Mod version: 1.20.2-3.2 (Modrinth App)


## **Description**
Hello, I noticed that items from other mods are saved incorrectly to the .txt file. For example, when I add an Enchanted Golden Apple (from vanilla Minecraft) as a custom drop for the Spider mob, it works as it should. However, when I add a drop from another mod, after a while the file (mobdropconfig.txt) rewrites itself and, instead of something like "myfoods\:enchanted\_golden\_bread", it becomes "minecraft\:air". This happens with every item that isn’t in the vanilla game.

issues.title: Options for how/when doors auto-open
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Forge

Mod name: Automatic Doors


## **Feature description**
Having the ability to control when door auto open would be useful for a number of reasons.

Options that give players some agency over the auto-opening behavior might include:
**A way to blanket disable in the config.** 
    Users who only want to be sure a door closes behind them would find this useful. They may want to have total control over opening doors and simply want door closing automated.
**Another option could be a key bind to toggle auto-opening off and on**.
    Gives users on the fly control, choosing between convenience and not wanting to disturb a creative build.
**Lastly, a 'barge in' mode**
    Doors auto open only while the player is sprinting; which is great since sprinters tend to be in a hurry (or a panic) and doors are clearly an obstacle to them.

All of these suggestions I make are based on times while I was using the mod, and had wanted for more control.

There's probably an endless number of reasons why a player may want to get close to a door but not open it. The fact that some have windows means you may just want to look out the door with it staying closed.

Some doors aren't meant to be opened, and instead are a decorative part of a build. These doors might have been left open to welcome guests. Builders love using doors in unique ways as well. Doors as fridges or a wadrobe, doors as a facade, doors as the back of chairs. It doesn't make sense to auto-open every door - and in a way Automatic Doors hampers the aesthetics for lack of control.

issues.title: Collective as a Dependency for my own mod
issues.body:
Hey,
I’m working on a utility mod for my modpack (which is MIT-licensed) and I noticed that the Collective mod has some really great utility and QoL features. Since Collective is under "All Rights Reserved," I know I can't copy its code, but I’m wondering how it works if I were to use Collective as a dependency for my mod, similar to how your mods rely on it.

I understand if it’s not possible, I just wanted to check before I start building my own implementations.
(if you do/don't allow this usage, you may want to mention it in the collective mod page so you don't get more questions like this)

issues.title: Feature Request: "Above Cut" Mode for Tree Harvester
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: Forge / Fabric / NeoForge

Mod name: Tree Harvester


## **Feature description**
First off, thanks for creating Tree Harvester — it has one of the best tree detection algorithms out there. It performs incredibly well, especially in large modpacks with tons of custom trees and mushrooms.

I'd love to suggest a feature inspired by another mod I enjoy using, [FallingTree](https://modrinth.com/mod/fallingtree). That mod includes an "above cut" mode, where only the blocks above the break point are harvested, leaving a trunk or stump behind.

It’s a subtle feature, but it adds a lot of visual charm — especially when dealing with large trees like 2×2 or 3×3 trunks. I think implementing something similar in Tree Harvester would be a great fit, especially given how well your mod handles tree structures from other mods.

Thanks again for your hard work, and I hope you consider adding this!

issues.title: Offering theoretically "easy" and "hard" solutions to an age old issue with "Areas".
issues.body:
## **Information** (? This is unclear as to what you want me to enter here...)
Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: Forge / Fabric / Neoforge (Your MO these days)

Mod name: Areas

  ...Okay. Please hear me out.

  One of most frustrating problems of the Areas mod is that even a semi-logical person (such as myself) sees that the text in the wood sign informs the mod based on a radius system _from_ the sign. Unfortunately, the signs are placed by the mod seemingly at random in villages, and hardly ever near the center of the village where a radius based detection system _SHOULD_ be placed to accommodate the area of the entire village accurately.

  So, _naturally_, I endeavoured to move the sign (!) to an estimated center of the village that I chose to stay at. I did this by either copying the sign's code before breaking it, then pasting the code back in at the new sign's location, _OR_ by using the "Carry-On" mod to _crouch right-click_, and pick the sign up intact, then place it elsewhere with the code untouched.

  The problem with all of this effort is that on reloading the world (for some reason I am ignorant of) the Areas mod replaces a sign back in the first sign's original location with a brand new random name, and the whole area gets messed up. 
  Apparently, editing the text is the only customization allowed presently.

  I offer you two possible solutions to this issue, of which you are welcome to use, pick at, pull apart or ignore at your pleasure:

1 - "**Easy**" (hypothetically) - You put an option in the config to turn off sign placement entirely. this would allow users to manually label village signs and make sure they are within approximate centrally locations without interference from Areas. They could visually estimate a fairly accurate central placement location, based on what size of village was generated for their specific world, and then they could adjust the radius size to properly surround the area they want included.  
( As a bonus, a sprite "ghost ring" could finally lets us SEE the radius for accurate inclusion, but that clearly raises the difficulty.)

2 - "**Hard**" - Make a proprietary white sign (I say 'white' only because it will make it much easier to find than a wood sign in a wood village with wood trees in tall grass, etc). This sign would be slightly larger than a standard wood sign, with 8 specific boxes for text: 1 box for the randomly generated area name, 1 blank box for a label of the area that the individual can enter (ie: 'village' of, 'hamlet' of, 'town' of, 'burrow' of, 'suburb' of etc... whatever they want), and then two rows of 3 small boxes to accommodate opposite corner coordinates. Areas could estimate these corner coordinates on spawn, and it wouldn't matter how inaccurate they are, as the user can walk around, get the coordinates they want, and input them in the sign. Moving the sign become irrelevant now as long as the sign stays within the inputted coordinates. If the sign is placed outside the signs inputted coordinates, the sign resets and the area is nameless again. The only reason now to want to move the sign at all would be for theoretical aesthetic reasons, but as long as the sign stays within the inputted coordinates, Areas won't have any need to replace the sign with a new one, and the sign could be placed wherever the user wants inside the bounds of the village. (sign<coordinates=good. lol)  
  This coordinate system would accommodate retrieving the exact bounding coordinates of an area that the user wants to name, allowing for much more creativity... such as designating named suburbs for a large city, or accommodating a few extra blocks around the outside of a village for an imposing defensive wall where the village name is announced on screen as you ride you horse through the portcullis! The accuracy and shear user control of this coordinate system makes me thrilled to think about all the creative possibilities.

I realize I am suggesting a lot of time consuming work, but my hope is you can see the potential of it, and might be excited to inject this irreplaceable, unique mod with some fresh new capabilities for all (me) to enjoy.   :)

Thank you for you time reading this and your consideration. I eagerly await your normal, automated reply bot. lol

Take care - PMZ (Mike)

issues.title: Option to add copper nuggets and modded metals to Mineral Chance
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1 / 1.21.1
Modloader: Forge

Mod name: Mineral Chance


## **Feature description**
### Specific Request
Presumably copper nuggets have been left out because there's so much copper in regular world generation. Have you considered adding an option to add it to the list as it is a vanilla nugget where appropriate (skyblock and other exotic world generation forms)?

### Generalization
More broadly, other mods add important metals, in my case I'm specifically thinking of Zinc for the Create mod, which is non-renewable. There is no mob that drops zinc, unlike copper and iron. Would you consider adding a configuration (or tag) where we could add more nuggets to the Overworld table, and another where we could add more nuggets to the nether table?

This ties back to #2982 - that request is about nerfing the table, this is about expanding it.

Exposing the tables in the config file instead of tags gives the secondary option of, eg, putting duplicate entries in the table to skew results.

**As a random example** 

- 10 for copper, 
- 50 for iron nuggets, 
- 5 for zinc nuggets, 
- 3 for gold nuggets, 
- 5 for lapis, 
- 5 for redstone, 
- 1 for emerald 
- 1 for diamond

### Advanced generalization
Make it a properly weighted table in the config file, so instead of copying and pasting iron nuggets 50 times and praying you didn't mess up a comma, you just put "50" next to it.

issues.title: [Mineral Chance] Option to replace gems with shards when available
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1 (and 1.21.1 pls)
Modloader: Forge

Mod name: Mineral Chance

## **Feature description**
Short: Give some way to use "partial gems" instead of full ones when provided by other mods.


### Problem
Dropping whole gems seems a little much, especially when I'm struggling along early game and get three diamonds before I get an iron pick. At least for game-play that emphasizes "getting sidetracked" from the main Minecraft progression to do another mods content. 

### Proposed Solution
Whole gems are dropped presumably because there's no such thing as a gem nugget?
Some mods add shards - representing partial gems the way nuggets are partial ingots. Typically either from mods that recycle/break down things and give partial returns, as side bonuses as part of refining something, or from "poor" ores. (Some of the "poor" ore mods might have another way of handling gems, IDK)

If a mod has registered their shards in (forge side) `forge:gems/diamond/shard`, `forge:gems/emerald/shard`, or `forge:gems/quartz/shard` can we have an option to dispense the first one from that tag instead? Possibly making the tag customizable - IDK what the tag is on Fabric side but I doubt it's in the forge namespace 😆 

### Another Proposed Solution
Can the list of minerals being dropped be in the config file, or be tag driven? These would allow more customization by mod-pack developers (or advanced users) but won't have the same drop-in effect that automatically pulling from the tags gives.

### Probably A Very Inconvenient Solution That Requires A Mod Rework
Change the drop table to be proportionate to ore generation in that chunk's biome.

issues.title: Request to Add Configuration File for Customizable Tracking Distance in Player Tracking Compass Mod
issues.body:
### **Information**  
- **Minecraft version:** 1.20.1  
- **Modloader:** Forge  
- **Mod name:** Player Tracking Compass  
- **Mod version:** 3.3  

---

### **Feature Request Description**  
The Tracking Compass is incredibly useful for locating players, but I would like to suggest adding a **configuration file** to allow users to customize the **minimum tracking distance threshold**.  

Currently, the compass stops tracking if other players are within a **10-block radius** (as stated in the mod description). However, some server environments or gameplay styles might benefit from adjusting this value. For example:  
- A server admin might want to increase the minimum distance to 20 blocks for a harder survival experience.  
- A player might want to reduce it to 5 blocks for cooperative gameplay.  

**Proposed Implementation:**  
- Add a config option (e.g., `minimumTrackingDistance` or `trackingRangeThreshold`) in the mod’s configuration file (e.g., `trackingcompass-config.toml`).  
- Ensure this value is reloadable (if possible) to adjust without restarting the game/server.  

This feature would greatly enhance the mod’s flexibility and adaptability to different use cases. Thank you for considering this request!  

---

### **Additional Notes**  
- The current behavior (default 10 blocks) should remain if the config option is not modified.  
- Compatibility with Forge’s config system (e.g., in-game GUI or manual file editing) would be ideal.  

Let me know if further details are needed! 😊

Once the timer expires, the spawner emits an explosion (or similar effect), destroying all attached torches and reactivating the spawner. This adds a strategic element, forcing players to periodically replace torches or risk spawner reactivation.

issues.title: Anvil Restoration Balancing
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.21.x
Modloader: Fabric

Mod name: Anvil Restoration


## **Feature description**
I like the QoL this mod adds, but 1 Iron Ingot to repair a full level of damage seems a bit too cheap. 1 Iron Block per repair seems, to me, like a more balanced cost (9 total Iron Ingots per repair level vs. 31 total Iron Ingots to craft a new Anvil). Also, given that there are 3 levels of integrity and the recipe for the Anvil requires 3 Iron Blocks, 1 Iron Block per repair just feels right to me.

I recognize that others may be used to this mod as-is and wouldn't appreciate a nerf, and I'm sure not everyone agrees with my reasoning. So I suppose the best option would be a config file with a configurable cost (something like "repairCost" : IRON-INGOT, IRON-BLOCK..., etc.).

issues.title: Spiders Only make web underground
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.20.1
Modloader: Forge / Fabric forb

Mod name: SpidersProduceWebs

issues.title: Title: Placeholder %s Not Replaced With Player Name in Broadcasted Message
issues.body:
## **Information**
Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: NeoForge
Forge version: 21.1.93
Environment: Multiplayer Dedicated Server

Mod name: Collective + First Join Message
Mod version: collective-1.21.1-7.87.jar + firstjoinmessage-1.21.1-3.6.jar


## **Description**
The configuration comment suggests that the string "%s" in serverBroadcastMessage is replaced by the player's username when they first join. However, the existing code does not perform this placeholder replacement. As a result, any %s inside the broadcast message appears literally in chat instead of showing the player's name.

**Steps to Reproduce**
Set the config to include %s, e.g. serverBroadcastMessage = "Welcome to the server, %s!".
Start the server and log in with a new player account.
Notice that the broadcast message literally shows %s instead of the player's username.

**Expected Behavior**
The broadcasted message should replace %s with the new player's username, e.g.:
"Welcome to the server, Steve!"

**Actual Behavior**
The broadcasted message still shows %s, e.g.:
Welcome to the server, %s!

**Possible Fix**
Manually replace %s in the code before broadcasting. For example, within the FirstSpawnEvent.java (or wherever the message is sent):

```
String customMessage = ConfigHandler.serverBroadcastMessage.replace("%s", player.getName().getString());
MessageFunctions.broadcastMessage(level, customMessage, colour);
```

issues.title: "Starter Kit" mod feature suggestion: Swap/Switch inventories
issues.body:
Add functionality for easy switching of inventories for all players. (Not just admin/op users.)

Minecraft version: 1.20.1 & 1.21.1
Modloader: Forge (1.20.1) & Neoforge (1.21.1)
(Probably most relevant to at least request it for the latest MC version at least, but I'm currently focussing on modpacks for 1.20.1 and 1.21.1.)

Mod name: Starter Kit

## **Feature description**
We have a multiplayer server and different friends that I sometimes play with.
In order to remain on the same "tech level" with specific friends, I'm currently manually switching my inventories every time when playing with the different friends, which is quite tedious and time consuming at the start of each gaming session.

Would it be possible to use the current functionality of "Starter Kit" to enable players to swap out their inventories with an existing kit and replace an existing kit with their current inventory inside the game?
Currently, I'm doing this manually as follows:
1. "/starterkit add Inventory1" (to create one for my current inventory)
2. "/starterkit activate Inventory2" (the previously saved inventory I want to load now)
3. "/starterkit give MyPlayerName Inventory2"
4. "/starterkit deactivate Inventory1" (to prevent a new player from randomly getting my inventory upon joining)
5. "/starterkit deactivate Inventory2" (to prevent a new player from randomly getting my inventory upon joining)

I'm aware of the Switchy mod out there, but that doesn't work in Forge without the Sinytra Connector mod, which is a bit heavy on the compatibility problems for me...

I also noticed that doing that kind of kit swapping doesn't affect the Curios items, so I still have to do some inventory swapping manually, but at least your mod is already making things a bit easier, which is why I thought you could perhaps add a command that does functionality like above in one line.

E.g:
1. "/starterkit AddSwapUserKit Inventory1" (creates a user + world specific kit called "Inventory1" with current inventory)
2. "/starterkit AddSwapUserKit Inventory2" (creates a user + world specific kit called "Inventory2" with current inventory)
3.  "/starterkit SwapUserKit From Inventory1 To Inventory2" (saves current inventory into Inventory1 and loads/gives Inventory2)
(From then on out, only step 3 will be needed whenever I need to switch.)

Alternatively, this might be better in a different mod of its own that either depends on Starter Kit or copies its coding to build something similar to how Switchy works, since teleporting to the last saved location or preserving experience as well as a part of the saved profile/kit might also be a nice extra feature, etc.

issues.title: Incompatibility: Ice Prevents Crop Growth & RpgDifficulty
issues.body:

Minecraft version: 1.21.1
Modloader: Fabric
Fabric loader version: 0.16..7
Environment: Multiplayer

First mod name: Ice Prevents Crop Growth
First mod version: 1.21.1-3.4

Second mod name: RpgDifficulty
Second mod version: 1.3.14


## **Description**
When both mods are on a server chunk loading can cause connection loss with a `Network Protocol Error`. Most often it happens when joining the server, unless the player is in an area without whatever mobs/entities seem to cause the error.
